Package neqsim.process.diagnostics

Class RelationshipGraph

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.diagnostics.RelationshipGraph
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class RelationshipGraph extends Object implements Serializable
Unsupervised lead-lag relationship discovery across historian tags.

Unlike EvidenceCollector, which only correlates tags a hypothesis already expects, this class scans all tag pairs in a historian data set with no symptom and no hypothesis supplied, and reports which tags move together and, crucially, which moves first. This gives an autonomous investigator the relationships it needs to form hypotheses on its own instead of being told what to look for.

For every unordered pair of tags (X, Y) the graph computes the Pearson correlation at a range of time lags and keeps the lag with the strongest absolute correlation. A positive optimal lag means X leads Y; the resulting RelationshipGraph.Relationship is stored as a directed edge from the leading (candidate cause) tag to the following (candidate effect) tag. Lead-lag directionality is the key signal that distinguishes a driver from a follower and lets downstream causal/topology reasoning promote a statistical edge to a causal candidate.

Usage example: 

 RelationshipGraph graph = new RelationshipGraph();
 graph.setTimestamps(timestamps); // optional, enables lag in seconds
 graph.setMaxLagSamples(10);
 graph.setMinAbsCorrelation(0.5);
 List<RelationshipGraph.Relationship> edges = graph.analyze(historianData);
 System.out.println(graph.toTextReport(edges));

    • setMaxLagSamples

      public void setMaxLagSamples(int maxLagSamples)
      Sets the maximum lag, in samples, searched in each direction.
      Parameters:
      maxLagSamples - maximum lag in samples; values below 0 are clamped to 0

    • setMinAbsCorrelation

      public void setMinAbsCorrelation(double minAbsCorrelation)
      Sets the minimum absolute correlation for a relationship to be reported.
      Parameters:
      minAbsCorrelation - threshold in range 0 to 1

    • setUseRankCorrelation

      public void setUseRankCorrelation(boolean useRankCorrelation)
      Enables or disables rank-based (Spearman) correlation.

      When enabled, each series is rank-transformed before correlation, so strong monotonic but non-linear couplings (e.g. a saturating or exponential response) are captured that a linear Pearson correlation would under-report.

      Parameters:
      useRankCorrelation - true to use rank (Spearman) correlation, false for linear (Pearson)

    • setTimestamps

      public void setTimestamps(double[] timestamps)
      Sets timestamps parallel to the historian arrays so lag can be expressed in seconds.

    • analyze

      public List<RelationshipGraph.Relationship> analyze(Map<String,double[]> data)
      Discovers lead-lag relationships across all tag pairs in the historian data.

      Returns:
      relationships ranked by descending absolute correlation; empty when fewer than two usable tags exist

    • bestLaggedRelationship

      private RelationshipGraph.Relationship bestLaggedRelationship(String tagX, double[] x, String tagY, double[] y, double medianDt)
      Finds the lag with the strongest absolute correlation for one tag pair and builds the directed relationship.
      Parameters:
      tagX - first tag name
      x - first time-series

      y - second time-series
      medianDt - median timestep in seconds, or NaN when unknown

      the best relationship for the pair, or null when no lag yields a valid correlation

    • pearsonLagged

      private double pearsonLagged(double[] a, double[] b, int lag)
      Computes the Pearson correlation between two series at a given integer lag, ignoring NaN pairs.

      A positive lag aligns a[i] with b[i + lag].

      Parameters:
      a - first series
      b - second series
      lag - integer lag in samples
      Returns:
      correlation in range -1 to 1, or NaN when fewer than 5 valid pairs overlap
